common-cold.name: Common Cold
common-cold.description: A mild viral infection of the upper respiratory tract that resolves naturally in 7-10 days.
general_care: Rest adequately and drink plenty of warm fluids.
Use steam inhalation or saline nasal spray.
Honey and warm water can soothe throat irritation.

influenza.name: Influenza
influenza.description: A contagious viral respiratory illness causing sudden onset of fever, severe body aches, and fatigue.
general_care: Rest in bed and stay well-hydrated.
Take paracetamol for fever and pain relief under medical advice.
Antiviral medications may help if taken within 48 hours.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.description: A chronic inflammatory airway condition causing reversible airflow obstruction and breathing difficulty.
general_care: Always carry your prescribed rescue inhaler.
Identify and avoid known environmental triggers (smoke, dust, pollen).
Track your peak expiratory flow rate if advised.

bronchitis.name: Bronchitis
bronchitis.description: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes usually following a cold or viral illness.
general_care: Drink warm fluids to thin bronchial secretions.
Use a room humidifier to soothe air passages.
Avoid active and passive cigarette smoke.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.description: A serious lung infection that causes air sacs to fill with fluid or pus.
general_care: Seek prompt medical diagnosis (chest X-ray/labs).
Complete the full course of prescribed antibiotics if bacterial.
Monitor oxygen saturation.

sinusitis.name: Sinusitis
sinusitis.description: Inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the sinuses, often causing facial pressure.
general_care: Apply warm facial compresses.
Perform gentle saline nasal rinses.
Stay hydrated to thin mucus.

copd.name: COPD
copd.description: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease causing long-term breathing difficulty and airflow blockage.
general_care: Strict smoking cessation.
Use prescribed bronchodilators and pulmonary rehab.
Avoid air pollutants and cold air.

pulmonary-embolism.name: Pulmonary Embolism
pulmonary-embolism.description: A blockage in one of the pulmonary arteries in your lungs, usually caused by blood clots from deep veins.
general_care: Seek emergency medical attention (Call 911/112 immediately).
Do not move excessively; remain seated.
Hospital anticoagulant therapy required.

laryngitis.name: Laryngitis
laryngitis.description: Inflammation of the vocal cords causing voice hoarseness and throat discomfort.
general_care: Rest your vocal cords; avoid whispering.
Drink warm soothing liquids and inhale steam.
Avoid smoking and alcohol.

pharyngitis.name: Pharyngitis
pharyngitis.description: Inflammation of the back of the throat, commonly known as a sore throat.
general_care: Gargle with warm salt water several times a day.
Drink warm soothing liquids.
Consult a doctor to test for Strep A bacterial infection.

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural Effusion
pleural-effusion.description: An unusual buildup of fluid between the layers of tissue that line the lungs and the chest cavity.
general_care: Seek medical evaluation and chest radiography.
Treat underlying cause (infection, heart failure).
Thoracentesis may be performed by specialists.

sleep-apnea.name: Sleep Apnea
sleep-apnea.description: A sleep disorder characterized by repeated interruptions in breathing throughout the sleep cycle.
general_care: Undergo a polysomnography sleep study.
Use a CPAP device as prescribed.
Maintain a healthy weight and avoid evening alcohol.

migraine.name: Migraine
migraine.description: A neurological condition characterized by recurrent, intense throbbing headaches typically on one side.
general_care: Rest in a dark, quiet room.
Apply a cold compress to the forehead.
Maintain consistent hydration and sleep schedules.

migraine-with-aura.name: Migraine with Aura
migraine-with-aura.description: Migraine headache accompanied by sensory or visual disturbances shortly before head pain starts.
general_care: Take prescribed acute migraine medication at the onset of aura.
Rest in a dimly lit room.
Avoid identified food or sensory triggers.

tension-headache.name: Tension Headache
tension-headache.description: The most common type of headache, feeling like a tight band wrapped around the head.
general_care: Apply heat or ice to neck and shoulders.
Practice stress-reduction and postural ergonomics.
Stay hydrated and take screen breaks.

cluster-headache.name: Cluster Headache
cluster-headache.description: Severe, sharp headaches that occur in cyclical patterns or clusters, typically centered around one eye.
general_care: High-flow oxygen therapy via non-rebreather mask.
Consult a neurologist for triptans and preventive calcium channel blockers.
Avoid alcohol during cluster periods.

epilepsy.name: Epilepsy
epilepsy.description: A central nervous system disorder in which brain activity becomes abnormal, causing seizures.
general_care: Take antiepileptic medications consistently without missing doses.
Keep seizure safety guidelines in mind.
Ensure adequate sleep and manage stress.

stroke.name: Stroke
stroke.description: A medical emergency where blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted or reduced.
general_care: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY (FAST Protocol).
Note the exact time symptoms started.
Do not give food, drink, or aspirin until evaluated.

transient-ischemic-attack-tia.name: Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
transient-ischemic-attack-tia.description: A temporary blockage of blood flow to the brain, serving as a critical warning sign for full stroke.
general_care: Seek emergency hospital evaluation immediately.
Undergo urgent brain imaging and vascular ultrasound.
Initiate stroke-prevention medication under specialist guidance.

multiple-sclerosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
multiple-sclerosis.description: An autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the protective sheath (myelin) covering nerve fibers.
general_care: Consult a neurologist for disease-modifying therapies (DMTs).
Engage in physical therapy.
Avoid extreme heat and fatigue.

parkinsons-disease.name: Parkinson's Disease
parkinsons-disease.description: A progressive nervous system disorder that affects movement, muscle control, and balance.
general_care: Work closely with a movement disorder specialist.
Maintain regular physical therapy and balance exercises.
Follow prescribed dopaminergic medication schedules.

trigeminal-neuralgia.name: Trigeminal Neuralgia
symptoms: pain triggered by chewing or brushing teeth
trigeminal-neuralgia.description: A chronic pain condition affecting the trigeminal nerve that carries sensation from the face to the brain.
general_care: Consult a neurologist for neuropathic pain modulators.
Avoid known facial touch triggers.
Consider neurosurgical evaluation if refractory.

bells-palsy.name: Bell's Palsy
bells-palsy.description: Sudden weakness or paralysis on one side of the face caused by inflammation of the 7th cranial nerve.
general_care: Consult a physician promptly for early corticosteroid therapy.
Use lubricating eye drops and an eye patch to protect the cornea.
Gentle facial physical therapy.

peripheral-neuropathy.name: Peripheral Neuropathy
peripheral-neuropathy.description: Damage to the peripheral nerves often causing tingling, numbness, and burning pain in hands and feet.
general_care: Optimize blood sugar management if diabetic.
Avoid tight restrictive footwear.
Consult a neurologist for nerve conduction studies.

gastritis.name: Gastritis
gastritis.description: Inflammation of the protective lining of the stomach, often caused by NSAIDs, H. pylori, or stress.
general_care: Eat smaller, frequent, non-irritating meals.
Avoid NSAID pain relievers, caffeine, alcohol, and spicy foods.
Antacids or acid suppressors can help.

gerd.name: GERD
gerd.description: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease causing chronic acid backflow into the esophagus.
general_care: Avoid lying down within 3 hours after meals.
Elevate the head of your bed 6 inches.
Limit citrus, chocolate, tomatoes, and carbonated beverages.

peptic-ulcer.name: Peptic Ulcer
peptic-ulcer.description: Open sores that develop on the inside lining of the stomach and the upper portion of the small intestine.
general_care: Get tested for Helicobacter pylori infection.
Avoid ibuprofen, naproxen, and aspirin.
Seek immediate care if vomit looks like coffee grounds or stools are black.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.description: A medical emergency involving acute inflammation of the appendix requiring immediate surgical attention.
general_care: GO TO THE EMERGENCY ROOM IMMEDIATELY.
Do NOT eat, drink, or take pain relievers/laxatives before surgical evaluation.
Do not apply heat to the abdomen.

gastroenteritis.name: Gastroenteritis
gastroenteritis.description: Intestinal infection commonly called stomach flu, marked by diarrhea, cramps, nausea, and fever.
general_care: Drink oral rehydration solution (ORS) and electrolyte broths in small sips.
Eat bland foods (bananas, rice, applesauce, toast - BRAT diet).
Seek care if unable to hold liquids for 24h.

irritable-bowel-syndrome.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
irritable-bowel-syndrome.description: A common gastrointestinal disorder that affects the large intestine causing chronic cramping and bowel changes.
general_care: Follow a low-FODMAP dietary approach under supervision.
Increase soluble fiber intake gradually.
Manage stress and maintain regular physical activity.

celiac-disease.name: Celiac Disease
celiac-disease.description: An autoimmune reaction to eating gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.
general_care: Adopt a strict lifelong gluten-free diet.
Consult a gastroenterologist for antibody testing and biopsy.
Take nutritional supplements for deficiencies.

gallstones.name: Gallstones
symptoms: sudden severe pain in upper right abdomen
gallstones.description: Hardened deposits of digestive fluid that form in your gallbladder, triggering biliary colic.
general_care: Seek medical evaluation (abdominal ultrasound).
Avoid high-fat and fried meals.
Seek immediate care if pain persists past 4 hours or fever develops.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
symptoms: severe upper abdominal pain radiating to back
pancreatitis.description: Inflammation of the pancreas that occurs when digestive enzymes become activated while still in the pancreas.
general_care: Seek emergency medical hospital admission.
Fast from food and drink initially to rest the pancreas.
Strictly abstain from alcohol.

constipation.name: Constipation
constipation.description: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements typically defined as fewer than three times a week.
general_care: Increase dietary fiber (chia seeds, prunes, vegetables).
Drink at least 2.5 liters of water daily.
Engage in regular physical walking.

diverticulitis.name: Diverticulitis
symptoms: constant severe lower left abdominal pain
diverticulitis.description: Inflammation or infection of small pouches (diverticula) that develop along the walls of the intestines.
general_care: Consult a doctor promptly for diagnostic imaging and antibiotics.
Temporarily switch to a clear liquid diet during acute flare.
Gradually reintroduce high-fiber foods.
diverticulitis.source: American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons

hemorrhoids.name: Hemorrhoids
hemorrhoids.description: Swollen veins in the lowest part of your rectum and anus.
general_care: Take warm sitz baths for 15 minutes twice daily.
Use high-fiber diet and stool softeners to avoid straining.
Apply topical hydrocortisone creams.

fatty-liver-disease.name: Fatty Liver Disease
symptoms: dull discomfort in upper right abdomen
fatty-liver-disease.description: Accumulation of excess fat in liver cells, commonly associated with metabolic syndrome or lifestyle.
general_care: Gradual, healthy weight reduction through Mediterranean diet.
Engage in 150 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly.
Avoid alcohol and sugary beverages.

hepatitis-a.name: Hepatitis A
hepatitis-a.description: A contagious liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus, usually transmitted via contaminated food or water.
general_care: Rest completely and avoid alcohol or liver-toxic drugs.
Drink plenty of clean fluids and eat nutritious small meals.
Strict hand hygiene to prevent spread.

crohns-disease.name: Crohn's Disease
crohns-disease.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that affects the lining of the digestive tract.
general_care: Consult a gastroenterologist for biologics or immunosuppressants.
Eat small frequent meals and track food triggers.
Stay hydrated and supplement vitamins.

ulcerative-colitis.name: Ulcerative Colitis
ulcerative-colitis.description: An inflammatory bowel disease that causes long-lasting inflammation and ulcers in your digestive tract's colon.
general_care: Adhere to prescribed anti-inflammatory maintenance medications.
Monitor iron levels and nutritional status.
Consult your specialist for regular colonoscopy.

malaria.name: Malaria
malaria.description: A mosquito-borne infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, causing severe fever cycles.
general_care: Seek immediate medical blood smear / rapid antigen test.
Complete full course of artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT).
Use mosquito bed nets.

dengue-fever.name: Dengue Fever
dengue-fever.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing severe flu-like illness, known colloquially as breakbone fever.
general_care: Maintain intensive hydration with electrolyte fluids.
Take paracetamol for fever; AVOID aspirin, ibuprofen, and NSAIDs.
Monitor platelet counts daily.

typhoid-fever.name: Typhoid Fever
typhoid-fever.description: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, spreading through contaminated food and drinking water.
general_care: Get blood/stool culture confirmation.
Take full course of prescribed antibiotics.
Drink exclusively purified or boiled water.

chikungunya.name: Chikungunya
chikungunya.description: A viral disease transmitted to humans by infected mosquitoes causing debilitating joint pain.
general_care: Rest and hydrate adequately.
Take analgesics and paracetamol for joint pain.
Gentle physical therapy during recovery.

chickenpox.name: Chickenpox
chickenpox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash and mild systemic fever.
general_care: Apply calamine lotion to soothe itching.
Take cool baths with baking soda or colloidal oatmeal.
Isolate until all blisters have crusted over.

shingles.name: Shingles
symptoms: fluid-filled blisters on one side of body
shingles.description: A reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus causing a painful, localized blistering rash.
general_care: Consult a doctor within 72h for antiviral therapy (acyclovir/valacyclovir).
Keep the rash clean and covered with non-stick dressings.
Apply cool wet compresses.

tuberculosis.name: Tuberculosis
symptoms: persistent cough for more than 3 weeks
tuberculosis.description: A serious bacterial infection that mainly affects the lungs, transmitted through airborne droplets.
general_care: Seek immediate sputum testing and chest radiography.
Strictly complete the 6-month multi-drug antibiotic regimen.
Wear a mask and ensure good room ventilation.

covid-19.name: COVID-19
covid-19.description: A contagious respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus.
general_care: Isolate in a well-ventilated room and monitor pulse oximeter readings.
Stay hydrated and get plenty of rest.
Seek emergency care if oxygen saturation drops below 94%.

hepatitis-b.name: Hepatitis B
hepatitis-b.description: A viral infection that attacks the liver, transmitted through infected blood or bodily fluids.
general_care: Consult a hepatologist for viral load and liver function tests.
Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic medications.
Family members should receive Hepatitis B vaccination.

hepatitis-c.name: Hepatitis C
hepatitis-c.description: A blood-borne viral infection that causes liver inflammation, often asymptomatic for decades.
general_care: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) medications can cure >95% of cases.
Get screened with an HCV antibody test.
Avoid all alcohol consumption.

mononucleosis.name: Mononucleosis
mononucleosis.description: A contagious viral illness commonly caused by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), spread through saliva.
general_care: Get plenty of bed rest and drink fluids.
Avoid contact sports or heavy lifting for 1 month to prevent spleen rupture.
Use throat lozenges and warm salt gargles.

lyme-disease.name: Lyme Disease
lyme-disease.description: A tick-borne bacterial illness caused by Borrelia burgdorferi transmitted by blacklegged ticks.
general_care: Consult a doctor promptly for early oral doxycycline antibiotic treatment.
Check skin for ticks after outdoor activities.
Monitor for joint pain or neurological signs.

measles.name: Measles
measles.description: A highly contagious airborne viral disease causing high fever and a full-body blotchy rash.
general_care: Strict isolation to prevent spreading.
Vitamin A supplementation under medical guidance.
Drink plenty of fluids and rest in dim lighting.

cholera.name: Cholera
cholera.description: An acute diarrheal illness caused by infection of the intestine with Vibrio cholerae bacteria.
general_care: IMMEDIATE and aggressive Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and IV fluids.
Seek emergency inpatient hospital stabilization.
Antibiotic therapy under medical supervision.

rabies-exposure.name: Rabies Exposure
rabies-exposure.description: A fatal viral disease transmitted through the saliva of infected animals (dogs, bats, raccoons).
general_care: WASH BITE WOUND WITH SOAP AND RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES IMMEDIATELY.
Seek emergency Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) vaccination without delay.
Do not wait for symptoms to appear.

hypertension.name: Hypertension
hypertension.description: Chronic high blood pressure where long-term force of blood against artery walls is elevated.
general_care: Adopt the DASH dietary pattern (low sodium, high potassium).
Engage in 30 minutes of daily aerobic exercise.
Take antihypertensive medication consistently as prescribed.

coronary-artery-disease.name: Coronary Artery Disease
symptoms: pain radiating to jaw or left arm
coronary-artery-disease.description: Narrowing or blockage of the coronary arteries usually caused by the buildup of cholesterol plaque.
general_care: Consult a cardiologist for ECG, stress test, and lipid profile.
Maintain heart-healthy Mediterranean diet.
Strictly control blood pressure and cholesterol.

heart-attack.name: Heart Attack
symptoms: pain radiating to left arm neck or jaw
heart-attack.description: A life-threatening medical emergency where blood flow to a section of heart muscle becomes blocked.
general_care: CALL EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (911/112) IMMEDIATELY.
Chew one regular 325mg aspirin if advised and not allergic.
Rest quietly in a semi-upright seated position.

arrhythmia.name: Arrhythmia
arrhythmia.description: An irregular heart rhythm where the heart beats too quickly, too slowly, or with an irregular pattern.
general_care: Consult a cardiologist for Holter monitoring and 12-lead ECG.
Limit caffeine, alcohol, and energy drinks.
Learn vagal maneuvers if advised by your physician.

heart-failure.name: Heart Failure
symptoms: shortness of breath when lying flat
heart-failure.description: A chronic condition in which the heart muscle cannot pump blood as efficiently as it should.
general_care: Weigh yourself daily and report sudden 2kg increases.
Adhere strictly to sodium (<2g/day) and fluid restrictions.
Take prescribed ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, or diuretics.

angina-pectoris.name: Angina Pectoris
symptoms: squeezing chest pain with physical exertion
pressure in chest relieved by rest
angina-pectoris.description: Chest pain or discomfort caused when heart muscle doesn't receive enough oxygen-rich blood during exertion.
general_care: Stop physical exertion and rest immediately.
Take sublingual nitroglycerin as prescribed.
Seek emergency care if pain lasts >5 minutes at rest.

pericarditis.name: Pericarditis
symptoms: sharp chest pain worse when lying down
pain relieved by sitting up and leaning forward
pericarditis.description: Inflammation of the pericardium (the fibrous sac surrounding the heart).
general_care: Seek medical evaluation and echocardiography.
Rest and avoid strenuous exercise.
Take prescribed anti-inflammatory medications (colchicine/NSAIDs).

deep-vein-thrombosis.name: Deep Vein Thrombosis
symptoms: swelling in one calf or leg
deep-vein-thrombosis.description: A blood clot that forms in a deep vein, usually in the lower legs, posing a risk of pulmonary embolism.
general_care: Seek urgent medical ultrasound evaluation.
Do NOT massage or vigorously rub the swollen leg.
Anticoagulant therapy is required.

peripheral-artery-disease.name: Peripheral Artery Disease
symptoms: coldness in lower leg or foot
peripheral-artery-disease.description: Narrowed arteries that reduce blood flow to the limbs, most commonly the lower extremities.
general_care: Smoking cessation is critical.
Engage in supervised walking exercise programs.
Inspect feet daily for wounds or pressure sores.

aortic-stenosis.name: Aortic Stenosis
aortic-stenosis.description: Narrowing of the aortic valve opening, restricting blood flow from the left ventricle to the aorta.
general_care: Consult a cardiologist for regular echocardiogram monitoring.
Avoid heavy isometric lifting.
Discuss surgical or TAVR valve replacement with specialists.

postural-orthostatic-tachycardia-pots.name: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia (POTS)
postural-orthostatic-tachycardia-pots.description: A condition where heart rate increases by over 30 bpm when transitioning from lying to standing, without significant BP drop.
general_care: Increase oral fluid intake (2.5-3L/day) and sodium under medical guidance.
Wear medical-grade compression stockings.
Engage in recumbent rowing/swimming exercises.

diabetes-type-1.name: Diabetes Type 1
diabetes-type-1.description: A chronic autoimmune condition in which the pancreas produces little or no insulin.
general_care: Daily blood glucose monitoring and insulin administration.
Count dietary carbohydrates accurately.
Check for urine ketones if blood sugar is persistently high.

diabetes-type-2.name: Diabetes Type 2
diabetes-type-2.description: A metabolic disorder characterized by high blood sugar, insulin resistance, and relative lack of insulin.
general_care: Adopt a low-glycemic, fiber-rich whole foods diet.
Exercise for at least 150 minutes per week.
Monitor HbA1c every 3-6 months with your doctor.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.description: An underactive thyroid gland that does not produce enough crucial thyroid hormone.
general_care: Take prescribed levothyroxine consistently on an empty stomach.
Get thyroid function blood tests (TSH/Free T4) checked periodically.
Eat a balanced iodine-sufficient diet.

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism
hyperthyroidism.description: An overactive thyroid gland producing an excess of thyroid hormone, speeding up metabolism.
general_care: Consult an endocrinologist for anti-thyroid medication (methimazole) or beta-blockers.
Avoid excess iodine and caffeine.
Protect eyes if thyroid eye disease is present.

cushings-syndrome.name: Cushing's Syndrome
cushings-syndrome.description: A metabolic disorder caused by prolonged exposure to high levels of cortisol hormone.
general_care: Consult an endocrinologist for 24-hour urinary cortisol testing.
Gradual tapering of exogenous steroid medications if applicable.
Monitor bone density and blood pressure.

addisons-disease.name: Addison's Disease
addisons-disease.description: Adrenal insufficiency where the adrenal glands produce insufficient cortisol and aldosterone.
general_care: Take lifelong hormone replacement therapy (hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone).
Carry an emergency medical alert ID card and injectable hydrocortisone.
Increase salt intake during hot weather or illness.

gout.name: Gout
symptoms: sudden intense joint pain in big toe
swelling and redness of big toe
gout.description: A painful form of inflammatory arthritis caused by the crystallization of uric acid in joints.
general_care: Apply ice packs and rest the inflamed joint.
Avoid purine-rich foods (red meat, shellfish, alcohol, beer).
Stay well-hydrated to help kidneys excrete uric acid.

metabolic-syndrome.name: Metabolic Syndrome
metabolic-syndrome.description: A cluster of metabolic risk factors that increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, and diabetes.
general_care: Achieve 7-10% weight reduction through balanced dietary caloric deficit.
Engage in daily brisk walking and resistance training.
Annual lipid and fasting glucose screenings.
metabolic-syndrome.source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

polycystic-ovary-syndrome.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.description: A hormonal disorder common among women of reproductive age causing enlarged ovaries with small cysts.
general_care: Adopt an anti-inflammatory, insulin-sensitizing diet.
Consult a gynecologist/endocrinologist for hormonal or metformin therapies.
Regular cardiovascular and metabolic checkups.

hypoglycemia.name: Hypoglycemia
hypoglycemia.description: An abnormally low level of blood sugar (glucose), body's main energy source, common in diabetic therapy.
general_care: Follow the 15-15 rule: Consume 15 grams of fast-acting carbs (juice, glucose tablets) and recheck in 15 minutes.
Always carry fast-acting glucose.
Review medication dosing with doctor.

urinary-tract-infection.name: Urinary Tract Infection
urinary-tract-infection.description: A bacterial infection of the urinary tract, most commonly affecting the bladder and urethra.
general_care: Drink abundant water to help flush bacteria.
Complete the full course of prescribed antibiotics.
Avoid holding urine for extended periods.

kidney-stones.name: Kidney Stones
symptoms: pain radiating to lower abdomen and groin
kidney-stones.description: Hard deposits made of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys and cause excruciating pain when passing.
general_care: Drink 3 to 4 liters of water daily to facilitate stone passage.
Take pain relief and alpha-blockers as prescribed by a urologist.
Strain urine to collect passed stones for analysis.

chronic-kidney-disease.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
chronic-kidney-disease.description: Gradual loss of kidney function over time, impairing the body's ability to filter waste from blood.
general_care: Strictly manage blood pressure and blood sugar levels.
Follow a kidney-friendly diet (controlled protein, sodium, potassium).
Consult a nephrologist regularly.

acute-cystitis.name: Acute Cystitis
acute-cystitis.description: Sudden bacterial inflammation of the urinary bladder.
general_care: Take prescribed antibiotics for the full recommended duration.
Stay well-hydrated with water.
Apply a warm heating pad to lower abdomen.

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.description: Age-associated non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland in men, causing urinary obstruction.
general_care: Avoid fluids 2 hours before bedtime.
Limit caffeine and alcohol intake.
Consult a urologist for alpha-blockers or 5-ARIs.

glomerulonephritis.name: Glomerulonephritis
glomerulonephritis.description: Inflammation of the tiny filters in your kidneys (glomeruli), which remove excess fluid, electrolytes, and waste.
general_care: Undergo urinalysis, kidney function blood tests, and renal biopsy.
Control blood pressure and reduce sodium intake.
Immunosuppressive therapy if autoimmune.

pyelonephritis.name: Pyelonephritis
pyelonephritis.description: A severe bacterial kidney infection typically ascending from a lower urinary tract infection.
general_care: Seek prompt medical care for targeted antibiotic therapy.
Inpatient IV antibiotics may be required for severe cases.
Maintain abundant oral or IV hydration.

interstitial-cystitis.name: Interstitial Cystitis
interstitial-cystitis.description: A chronic, painful bladder condition characterized by bladder pressure and pelvic pain without infection.
general_care: Avoid dietary bladder irritants (coffee, tomatoes, artificial sweeteners).
Undergo physical therapy for pelvic floor muscles.
Consult a urologist for bladder instillation therapy.

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
symptoms: joint pain during or after movement
osteoarthritis.description: The most common form of arthritis, occurring when protective cartilage on the ends of bones wears down over time.
general_care: Engage in low-impact exercises (swimming, stationary cycling).
Maintain a healthy weight to reduce joint load.
Use hot/cold therapy for joint comfort.

rheumatoid-arthritis.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
symptoms: symmetrical joint pain in both hands
rheumatoid-arthritis.description: A chronic autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints symmetrically, causing painful swelling and bone erosion.
general_care: Consult a rheumatologist for Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs (DMARDs).
Engage in gentle range-of-motion physical therapy.
Balance activity with restorative joint rest.

fibromyalgia.name: Fibromyalgia
fibromyalgia.description: A disorder characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain accompanied by fatigue, sleep, memory, and mood issues.
general_care: Maintain gentle regular aerobic exercise (walking, water aerobics).
Practice sleep hygiene and stress-reduction techniques.
Medications like duloxetine or pregabalin under doctor guidance.

sciatica.name: Sciatica
symptoms: sharp shooting pain from lower back down leg
sciatica.description: Pain radiating along the path of the sciatic nerve, which branches from your lower back through your hips and down each leg.
general_care: Apply alternating ice and warm packs to the lower back.
Practice gentle hamstring and lower back stretching exercises.
Avoid prolonged seated positions.

tendinitis.name: Tendinitis
symptoms: dull ache when moving affected tendon
joint stiffness near shoulder elbow or heel
tendinitis.description: Inflammation or irritation of a tendon, commonly affecting shoulders, elbows (tennis elbow), or Achilles tendon.
general_care: Follow RICE protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
Temporarily avoid activities that trigger tendon strain.
Physiotherapy for eccentric strengthening.

carpal-tunnel-syndrome.name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
symptoms: numbness and tingling in thumb index and middle fingers
carpal-tunnel-syndrome.description: Compression of the median nerve as it travels through the carpal tunnel in the wrist.
general_care: Wear a supportive wrist splint, especially at night.
Take ergonomic breaks during typing or repetitive hand tasks.
Consult a doctor for nerve conduction study.

ankylosing-spondylitis.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis
symptoms: chronic lower back pain and stiffness
pain worse in mornings and improves with exercise
ankylosing-spondylitis.description: An inflammatory arthritis that causes some of the vertebrae in the spine to fuse over time.
general_care: Consult a rheumatologist for biologic therapies (TNF inhibitors).
Daily spinal stretching and posture exercises.
Swimming is highly recommended.

bursitis.name: Bursitis
symptoms: swelling and redness over shoulder elbow or hip
bursitis.description: Painful condition that affects the small, fluid-filled sacs (bursae) that cushion the bones, tendons, and muscles.
general_care: Rest and immobilize the affected joint temporarily.
Apply cold compresses for 20 minutes several times a day.
Use cushioning pads over pressure points.

osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis
symptoms: gradual loss of height over time
back pain caused by collapsed vertebra
osteoporosis.description: A bone disease that occurs when the body loses too much bone, causing bones to become weak and brittle.
general_care: Ensure adequate calcium (1200mg) and Vitamin D (800-1000 IU) intake.
Engage in weight-bearing and balance exercises.
Undergo DXA bone mineral density screening.

cervical-spondylosis.name: Cervical Spondylosis
symptoms: tingling or numbness in arms or fingers
headache starting at back of neck
cervical-spondylosis.description: Age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in your neck (cervical spine).
general_care: Practice ergonomic workstation alignment with screen at eye level.
Perform gentle neck stretching and physical therapy exercises.
Use a supportive ergonomic cervical pillow.

eczema.name: Eczema
eczema.description: A chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by dry, itchy, and irritated patches.
general_care: Moisturize skin liberally twice daily with fragrance-free thick ointments.
Take brief lukewarm baths and avoid harsh detergents.
Use topical corticosteroid creams during flares as prescribed.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
symptoms: red skin patches covered with thick silvery scales
dry cracked skin that may bleed
psoriasis.description: An autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the growth cycle of skin cells, leading to thick silvery plaques.
general_care: Apply prescribed topical vitamin D or corticosteroid ointments.
Keep skin moisturized to prevent cracking.
Consult a dermatologist for phototherapy or biologics.

acne-vulgaris.name: Acne Vulgaris
acne-vulgaris.description: A common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells.
general_care: Cleanse face gently twice daily with non-comedogenic cleanser.
Use over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid.
Consult a dermatologist for topical retinoids.

urticaria.name: Urticaria
symptoms: swelling that changes shape and location
urticaria.description: Hives triggered by allergic reactions, physical pressure, temperature changes, or viral infections.
general_care: Take non-drowsy oral antihistamines (cetirizine, fexofenadine).
Apply cool damp cloths to soothe itchy areas.
Avoid hot showers and tight clothing.
urticaria.source: American College of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology

fungal-skin-infection.name: Fungal Skin Infection
symptoms: circular red itchy rash with raised edges
clear skin in center of ring
fungal-skin-infection.description: Superficial fungal infection of the skin commonly called ringworm, athlete's foot, or jock itch.
general_care: Apply over-the-counter topical antifungal cream (clotrimazole, terbinafine) for 2-4 weeks.
Keep affected area clean and completely dry.
Avoid sharing personal towels or clothing.

contact-dermatitis.name: Contact Dermatitis
symptoms: red rash localized to area of contact
contact-dermatitis.description: A red, itchy rash caused by direct contact with a substance or an allergic reaction to it (e.g. nickel, poison ivy, soaps).
general_care: Identify and strictly avoid the offending trigger substance.
Wash affected skin immediately with mild soap and water.
Apply cold compresses and calamine lotion.

rosacea.name: Rosacea
symptoms: facial redness across cheeks and nose
rosacea.description: A common chronic skin condition that causes blushing or flushing and visible blood vessels in your face.
general_care: Wear daily broad-spectrum SPF 50+ mineral sunscreen.
Avoid known triggers (spicy food, hot beverages, alcohol, extreme weather).
Use gentle, fragrance-free skincare products.

alopecia-areata.name: Alopecia Areata
symptoms: round coin-sized smooth bald patches on scalp
alopecia-areata.description: An autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks hair follicles, causing patchy hair loss.
general_care: Consult a dermatologist for intralesional corticosteroid injections.
Protect bald scalp patches from sun exposure with hats/SPF.
Join support communities.

scabies.name: Scabies
symptoms: thin wavy burrow tracks on skin
tiny blisters between fingers wrists and waistline
scabies.description: An infestation of the skin by the human itch mite (Sarcoptes scabiei), causing severe nighttime itching.
general_care: Apply prescription 5% permethrin cream from neck to toes overnight.
Wash all bedding, towels, and clothing in hot water.
Treat all close household contacts simultaneously.

cellulitis.name: Cellulitis
cellulitis.description: A potentially serious bacterial skin infection affecting deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue.
general_care: Seek prompt medical evaluation for oral or IV antibiotics.
Elevate the affected limb to reduce swelling.
Mark the border of redness with a pen to monitor progression.

impetigo.name: Impetigo
symptoms: red sores around nose and mouth
sores rupture and form honey-colored crusts
impetigo.description: A highly contagious bacterial skin infection common in young children and infants.
general_care: Apply prescribed topical antibiotic ointment (mupirocin).
Gently wash sores with mild soap and warm water.
Keep fingernails short to prevent scratching and spread.

iron-deficiency-anemia.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
symptoms: shortness of breath with mild exertion
iron-deficiency-anemia.description: A condition where blood lacks adequate healthy red blood cells due to insufficient iron.
general_care: Eat iron-rich foods (lean meat, lentils, spinach, fortified cereals).
Take iron supplements with vitamin C (orange juice) to enhance absorption.
Avoid drinking tea or coffee with meals.

vitamin-d-deficiency.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
vitamin-d-deficiency.description: Inadequate levels of vitamin D in the body, impairing calcium absorption and immune health.
general_care: Get 15-20 minutes of safe midday sun exposure.
Take vitamin D3 supplements as prescribed based on 25-OH vitamin D levels.
Consume fortified milk, fatty fish, and egg yolks.

vitamin-b12-deficiency.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
vitamin-b12-deficiency.description: Insufficient vitamin B12 leading to anemia and nerve damage, common in vegans, elderly, or malabsorption.
general_care: Take oral or sublingual methylcobalamin B12 supplements.
Consume fortified nutritional yeast, dairy, or meat.
Consult a doctor for B12 injections if malabsorptive.
vitamin-b12-deficiency.source: National Institutes of Health (NIH) — Vitamin B12

dehydration.name: Dehydration
dehydration.description: A dangerous condition that occurs when you lose more fluids than you take in.
general_care: Drink oral rehydration salts (ORS) or electrolyte solutions in small regular sips.
Avoid caffeinated or sugary energy drinks.
Seek emergency IV fluids if unable to retain fluids.

electrolyte-imbalance.name: Electrolyte Imbalance
electrolyte-imbalance.description: Disruption in the normal concentration of essential minerals (sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium) in the blood.
general_care: Consume balanced electrolyte broths or drinks.
Undergo a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP) blood test.
Do not take potassium supplements without physician authorization.

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
symptoms: petechiae (superficial pinpoint purple spots on skin)
thrombocytopenia.description: An abnormally low level of platelets (thrombocytes) in the blood, impairing normal blood clotting.
general_care: Consult a hematologist for complete blood count (CBC).
Avoid contact sports and heavy trauma.
Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, and other blood-thinning NSAIDs.
thrombocytopenia.source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

scurvy.name: Scurvy
scurvy.description: A disease caused by severe lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) in the diet.
general_care: Consume daily fresh citrus fruits (oranges, lemons), kiwi, bell peppers, and strawberries.
Take oral Vitamin C supplements.
Symptoms typically reverse rapidly with supplementation.

thalassemia-minor.name: Thalassemia Minor
symptoms: microcytic red blood cells on lab work
thalassemia-minor.description: An inherited blood disorder that causes the body to have less hemoglobin and smaller red blood cells.
general_care: Undergo hemoglobin electrophoresis for formal confirmation.
Genetic counseling before family planning.
Do not take iron supplements unless iron deficiency is proven by ferritin test.

otitis-media.name: Otitis Media
otitis-media.description: An infection of the middle ear, the air-filled space behind the eardrum containing vibrating bones.
general_care: Apply a warm moist cloth over the affected ear.
Take pain relievers (paracetamol/ibuprofen) as recommended.
Consult an ENT doctor if ear discharge occurs.

allergic-rhinitis.name: Allergic Rhinitis
allergic-rhinitis.description: An allergic response to airborne allergens such as pollen, pet dander, dust mites, or mold.
general_care: Use daily intranasal corticosteroid spray (fluticasone).
Take second-generation oral antihistamines (cetirizine/loratadine).
Keep windows closed during high pollen counts.

tonsillitis.name: Tonsillitis
symptoms: white or yellow coating on tonsils
tonsillitis.description: Inflammation of the tonsils, two oval-shaped pads of tissue at the back of the throat.
general_care: Gargle with warm salt water several times daily.
Sip warm soothing herbal teas with honey.
Consult a doctor for rapid strep swab to determine if antibiotics are needed.

conjunctivitis.name: Conjunctivitis
symptoms: pink or red discoloration of eye
conjunctivitis.description: Inflammation of the transparent membrane (conjunctiva) lining the eyelid and eyeball, commonly known as pink eye.
general_care: Apply cool compresses to closed eyelids.
Avoid touching or rubbing eyes and wash hands frequently.
Discard old eye makeup and clean contact lenses thoroughly.

dry-eye-syndrome.name: Dry Eye Syndrome
dry-eye-syndrome.description: A common condition that occurs when your tears aren't able to provide adequate lubrication for your eyes.
general_care: Use preservative-free artificial tear eye drops.
Follow the 20-20-20 rule during screen use (look 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes).
Use a room humidifier.

glaucoma.name: Glaucoma
symptoms: severe eye pain with halo around lights
glaucoma.description: A group of eye conditions that damage the optic nerve, often caused by abnormally high pressure in the eye.
general_care: Undergo regular comprehensive eye exams including tonometry.
Take prescribed pressure-lowering eye drops daily without fail.
Seek emergency care for sudden severe eye pain with vomiting.

cataract.name: Cataract
cataract.description: A clouding of the normally clear lens of your eye, leading to a decrease in vision.
general_care: Consult an ophthalmologist for regular visual acuity testing.
Use brighter task lighting when reading.
Cataract surgery is a safe, definitive outpatient curative procedure.

benign-paroxysmal-positional-vertigo.name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
symptoms: sudden spinning sensation when turning head
dizziness when rolling over in bed
benign-paroxysmal-positional-vertigo.description: A disorder arising from the inner ear characterized by repeated brief episodes of spinning vertigo.
general_care: Consult an ENT specialist or physical therapist for the Epley canalith repositioning maneuver.
Avoid sudden head movements.
Sit on the edge of the bed for 1 minute before standing.

generalized-anxiety-disorder.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
generalized-anxiety-disorder.description: Chronic, exaggerated worry and tension about everyday life events without obvious reasons for concern.
general_care: Practice daily mindfulness and diaphragmatic breathing.
Limit caffeine and alcohol intake.
Consult a mental health professional for Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT).
generalized-anxiety-disorder.source: Anxiety and Depression Association of America

major-depressive-disorder.name: Major Depressive Disorder
major-depressive-disorder.description: A mood disorder that causes a persistent feeling of sadness and loss of interest, affecting daily functioning.
general_care: Reach out to a trusted counselor, psychologist, or psychiatrist.
Engage in daily gentle walking and structured daily routines.
Seek emergency support if self-harm thoughts occur.

panic-disorder.name: Panic Disorder
panic-disorder.description: A type of anxiety disorder characterized by recurrent unexpected panic attacks.
general_care: Practice the 4-7-8 deep breathing technique during an attack.
Remind yourself that panic attacks peak in 10 minutes and will pass.
Consult a therapist for CBT.

insomnia-disorder.name: Insomnia Disorder
insomnia-disorder.description: A common sleep disorder that makes it hard to fall asleep, stay asleep, or causes non-restorative sleep.
general_care: Maintain a fixed sleep and wake-up time 7 days a week.
Avoid screens and blue light 1 hour before bed.
Keep bedroom cool, dark, and quiet.

social-anxiety-disorder.name: Social Anxiety Disorder
symptoms: fear of being judged or embarrassed
social-anxiety-disorder.description: An intense, persistent fear of being watched and judged by others in social and performance situations.
general_care: Gradual exposure therapy under professional psychological guidance.
Practice social interaction in low-stakes safe environments.
CBT is the gold-standard treatment.

chronic-stress---burnout.name: Chronic Stress / Burnout
chronic-stress---burnout.description: A state of emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged stress.
general_care: Establish clear work-life boundaries and scheduled offline downtime.
Engage in restorative hobbies and daily physical movement.
Speak with a counselor or occupational health specialist.
